Living-planet parameters — the procedural weather field
Sourcesrc/core\tokens\starfield\params\weather.ts
UX surfaceShared primitives every surface builds on — no direct UI.

Members

CLOUD_FREQ

Base fbm coverage frequency — sampled in unit-sphere space so the value counts octaves of planetary-scale features (2.8 ≈ continent- sized cloud banks with sub-structure).

CLOUD_DETAIL_FREQ

Detail octave — a second fbm layer at ~4× the base frequency that breaks coverage into clumpy, cauliflower-edged banks instead of smooth latitude stripes; DETAIL_GAIN is its blend weight.

CLOUD_EVOLVE

Noise-field evolution rate (scene-seconds⁻¹) — slow morph, no boil.

CLOUD_STEER

How much the real 8k cloud map steers procedural coverage (0..1).

COVER_LO

Coverage ramp edges — below LO is clear sky, above HI is overcast. A tight ramp punches broken cloud shapes out of the field; a wide soft ramp reads as haze stripes.

JET_BASE

Differential rotation — air masses shear against the surface: base equatorial drift plus a mid-latitude jet boost (lat-weighted so weather visibly races around the temperate bands, slow near the poles — the read that makes the planet feel alive in close orbit).

LAT_MEANDER

Latitude meander — slow noise that warps the coverage sample in the vertical direction so jet-sheared banks undulate north/south instead of ringing the globe in straight east-west stripes.

ITCZ_HALF

ITCZ — the equatorial convergence band where trade winds meet. HALF is the band half-width (radians of latitude), GAIN its extra cover, WANDER how far it migrates with the solar declination (monsoon seasonality — the band follows the sun north/south).

ITCZ_CELL_LO

Convective-cell gate for the ITCZ — the band only clouds where the detail octave beats this ramp, so the convergence zone renders as a broken chain of storm puffs instead of a solid equatorial stripe.

DENS_POW

Density→opacity power — thin noise haze is crushed toward zero so only genuine cloud mass renders; keeps the surface saturated under the deck.

STORM_N

Hurricane vortices — N seeded tropical cyclones; R is the chord radius of the storm envelope, GAIN its cover contribution, SWIRL the spiral-arm twist (radians at core), DRIFT the band-limited westward walk, FREQ the feeder-band noise frequency, EYE_R/DIP the calm eye punch-out.

ICE_BASE

Polar snow/ice — ICE_BASE is the northern solstice cap edge in |lat| units (0.82 ≈ 55°N keeps the cap polar instead of blanketing half the globe); ICE_DECL swings the line against the solar declination so the cap visibly grows into winter and retreats in summer. The south runs a tighter, steadier footprint — ICE_S_BASE keeps it poleward of ~64°S and ICE_S_DECL halves its seasonal swing, so southern glaciation never approaches the northern winter's reach. SNOW_GAIN is the cap's deck-brightness contribution — a fraction, not a coat.

VOLC_R

Volcanic ash — one seeded eruption site pulsing on a slow period; GAIN is plume darkness, VOLC_R its radius (unit-sphere chord), VOLC_PERIOD the eruption cycle in scene-seconds.

ASH_TINT

Ash plume tint — dark gray-brown against the white deck.

SHADOW

Cloud shadow — the fraction the surface dims under dense deck on the day side only (night lights must never be occluded).

SF_SOLAR_WIND

Solar-wind activity cycle — one shared uniform drives the sun's flare frequency AND every aurora shell, so a storm spike on the Sun visibly reaches Earth/Jupiter/Saturn/Neptune a beat later. BASE+WAVE give the slow ~11-year-style swell; the storm term multiplies two detuned sines and takes a high power so spikes stay rare and sharp.

BASE

Quiet-Sun floor of the wind uniform.

WAVE_AMP

Slow activity swell amplitude + period (scene-seconds).

STORM_F1

Storm spikes — product of two detuned sines to a high power lands a bright gust every ~90–140 s that lasts a few seconds; GAIN scales the spike on top of BASE+WAVE.

FLARE_N

Limb flares — N seeded prominence sprites on the Sun's equatorial band; each breathes at its own rate and stretches past the limb when the wind spikes.

(module scope)

Aurora shells — polar emission curtains on atmosphere-bearing bodies. Driven by the shared solar-wind uniform: quiet wind shows a faint oval shimmer, storms ignite bright rippling curtains.

LAT0

Auroral oval center — |lat| on the unit sphere (~0.8 ≈ 53° from the equator, the real auroral zone sits just inside the pole).

OVAL_W

Oval gaussian half-width — the emission is a thin curtain RING hugging the oval; wide windows read as a smeared cap (the old "green fried egg"), so this stays deliberately narrow.

LAT_WOBBLE

Oval waviness — substorm arcs buckle the ring with longitude; sampled as noise on the sphere so there's no seam at ±π.

FOLD_FREQ

Curtain folds — real auroral striation runs ACROSS the band (rays stand perpendicular to the arc), so the fold phase is the signed distance from the oval centerline, not longitude — from orbit this reads as woven ribbon filaments instead of radial spokes. FOLD_JAG slides the fold phase with noise along the oval so the ribbons curl and merge; FOLD_SHARP (a power) thins each filament's bright core; FOLD_DRIFT ripples the weave with time.

FOLD_FLOOR

Fold floor — gaps between filaments stay dimly lit.

ARC2_OFF

Secondary arc — real substorm ovals frequently run a fainter parallel arc poleward of the main one; ARC2_OFF is its latitude offset, ARC2_GAIN its relative brightness.

PATCH_FREQ

Arc patchiness — a medium-frequency mottle multiplies the oval so segments vary in brightness irregularly (patches, torch curls) instead of a smooth one-level arc.

ARC_FREQ

Arc breakup — low-frequency longitude modulation flares sections of the oval (auroral substorms brighten one sector at a time); ARC_GAIN is the modulation contrast — high values let sectors go dark so storms never wash the whole oval flat.

INTENSITY

Brightness scale against the wind uniform — a faint shimmer that storms multiply through wind, visible on the dark limb without reading as a second surface layer.

SHELL_SCALE

Shell lift above the surface radius — hugs the atmosphere top.

LIMB_POW

Limb-fade power — |view normal z| powered this high so the oval only glows when seen against the planet's face; at the silhouette the shell would otherwise draw arcs floating off the limb.

TILT

Default magnetic-axis tilt (radians) — Earth's dipole sits ~11° off the spin axis; per-body aurora.tilt overrides (Neptune's dipole is offset ~47°, swinging its oval wildly off-pole).

NIGHT_LO

Night-side gate — auroras read through darkness: dot(normal, sunDir) smoothstepped between the edges so day-side emission fades to DAY_FLOOR instead of vanishing (UV aurora still runs in sunlight, it just doesn't show).

HEMI_LO

Hemisphere gate — aurora.south === false fades the oval out across the magnetic equator so only the boreal (north) curtain shows; the giants keep both ovals. Edges are signed magnetic latitude on the unit sphere.

TOP

Default palette — oxygen-green curtain top over a violet-red lower edge (Earth); per-body aurora.color/colorLow override for the giants' hydrogen-dominated blues and cyans.

SF_METEOR

Meteor strikes — airless cratered bodies (Moon, Callisto, Mercury, the asteroid dwarfs) still take hits; a small pooled sprite flashes at a random surface point every few seconds, the way a real impact fireball flickers. Pool keeps allocation out of the frame loop.

INTERVAL

Mean seconds between strikes per body (per-strike jitter ±60%).

LIFE

Flash duration — rise fast (25% of life), decay slow.

SIZE

Flash sprite diameter × the body radius.

POOL

Sprites pooled per flagged body.

COLOR

Impact flash tint — hot white-gold impact fireball.

SF_CONSTELLATION

LEO constellation shell — the Starlink-class swarm: dozens of small lit specks sharing one inclined orbital plane that sweeps as a unit.

ORBIT

Shell altitude as a multiple of the body radius.

SPEED

Shell angular speed multiplier (frame pivot).

INCLINE

Orbital plane inclination (radians, ~53° like Starlink).

INCLINE_SPREAD

Inclination spread (radians) — real shells fly several planes (53°, 53.2°, 70°, 97.6° for Starlink), so per-satellite jitter around the base scatters the swarm into a volume instead of tracing a single crisp ring.

JITTER

Altitude jitter fraction — the shell has thickness, not a line.

SIZE

Point size vs the host body radius — glints, not balls.

REVEAL

Near-field reveal distance (world units) — LEO satellites are invisible from interplanetary range: the swarm resolves only when the camera is inside the Moon's orbital neighborhood (~4.5 units), so the threshold sits just past it. The value is an absolute camera-to-host distance, replacing the generic LOD PAD + size·SCALE reach that would otherwise key on the host's heliocentric orbit and reveal the shell from halfway across the chart.

SF_PLUME

Cryovolcanic/volcanic plume systems — Enceladus vents water-ice geysers from its south-polar tiger stripes, Io throws sulfur plumes hundreds of km over its whole surface. Each vent carries a steady jet sprite plus a rising puff sprite that cycles outward, fades, and recycles — a continuous eruption read without per-frame allocation.

VENTS

Default vent count when def.plumes.count is unset.

HEIGHT

Jet/puff reach as a multiple of the body radius.

WIDTH

Jet sprite width × body radius.

JET_BASE_W

Jet cone footprint — the steady column is an open-ended tapered cylinder rooted at the vent (narrow throat, umbrella spread at the top, CylinderGeometry(rTop>rBottom)). JET_SEG is the radial tessellation — 12 keeps the silhouette round under any azimuth. A vertical alpha gradient texture feeds map: blazing at the vent (v=1 side) and dissolving into transparency at the rim.

PERIOD

Rising-puff cycle seconds (per-vent phase is seeded).

OPACITY

Steady jet opacity at the vent base.

PUFF_OPACITY

Puff opacity peak at the bottom of its rise.

SUN_LO

Sunlight gate — cryovolcanic jets scatter sunlight, so a vent on the body's night side shows only a faint smudge. dot(ventDir, sunDirLocal) smoothsteps between LO/HI: fully dark vents keep DARK_FLOOR so the plume never pops discontinuously at the terminator.

POLAR_LAT

Polar vent latitude band — |y| on the unit sphere above this marks the tiger-stripe cluster (Enceladus vents sit ~75°S). Scattered (volcanic) vents ignore it and sample the whole sphere.

POLAR_SPREAD

Per-vent spread around the pole direction (unit-sphere radius).
